body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: f298637c81ad6be4c018742d8bd89f5d6ad884e1 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Built and tested on PR + main + the pending #844 fix (mkinney 2c05183c): main does not build right now (#844, `trochoid_slot.rs`), so the trial merge with main needed that fix to compile. A failure from #844 is not a finding against this PR.

**What looks good**
- Display only: the diff touches no law, verdict, post, command, MCP tool or snapshot PNG (`crates/ui/tests/snapshots` unchanged; no AGENTS.md, `.claude/`, `xtask/`, `.cargo/`, `scripts/` or `build.rs` change, so no PROCESS_VERSION bump is needed).
- The outline is built from the same two calls the fixture laws make: `tool_body::judged` then `tool_body::stack` (`crates/app/src/sim_tool_body.rs` `for_operation`, lines 147-160). The meridian is the cutter from `Tool::profile()` plus `holder_meridian()` of the same stack bands.
- Degenerate outlines return a named `OutlineError` and draw nothing; the UI logs once per distinct reason (`SimToolCache::tool_frame`, lines 193-199). No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` in non-test code (the only hits in the added lines are in the UI test).
- Cache freeing holds: `sim_tool_tris` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/world.rs`) clears the cache when no tool is at the playhead; `for_operation` returns `None` for a deleted op or tool, and a refused tool empties it. The `Mutex` is poison-tolerant (`unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)`).
- Layering holds: the mesh is generated in app; the viewport only posts and draws it. The UI passes `&state.world` to an app function, the same pattern the old `assembly_for_operation` call used.
- Tilted axis: `tool_body_view::posed` takes `sim::Frame::axis`; `the_body_follows_a_tilted_tool_axis` covers it.
- `sim_tool_body.rs` is 229 lines, both new test files are under 310 lines.

**Local results (trial merge + #844 fix, Windows, CARGO_TARGET_DIR per review)**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app --test sim_tool_body` | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-app --test tool_spun_profile` | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-app --test tool_body` | 8 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-app --test tool_body_view` | 12 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib tool_body` (CWD crates/ui) | 12 passed, 0 failed (incl. `the_simulation_draws_the_tool_with_its_holder_cylinder_or_its_body`) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Trial merge with origin/main textually clean. Without the #844 fix, `camcraft-motion` fails with the seven known `trochoid_slot.rs` errors (E0609/E0308), nothing else.

**Requested before merge**
None blocking.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. Dead code: `tool_body_view::assembly_for_operation` (`crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs:245`) has no callers anywhere in the tree. `bare_assembly` (line 232) is used only by `crates/app/tests/tool_body_view.rs:185,193`. Removing the first, or filing it as a follow-up, would keep the view module honest.
2. Per frame, not per change: the mesh is cached, but `for_operation` reads the body from the world (`tool_body::body_of` clones the `ToolBody`), runs `judged`/`stack` and rebuilds the `JudgedOutline` every frame to compare it. Cheap, but the decision doc's "rebuilt only when a judged number changes" holds for the mesh only.
3. Transport close frees the mesh lazily: `sim_tool_tris` clears it on the next scene collect, not in the close command itself. The structural test asserts it after `collect`, which is what the viewport does each frame, so this is fine in practice.
4. Provenance: the module header (`sim_tool_body.rs` lines 1-10) says "our own design, no vendor file or source consulted" but cites no public source for the solid-of-revolution construction, which AGENTS.md asks for. A one-line citation would do.
5. `crates/ui/src/state.rs` is already over 400 lines (4210); this PR adds 7 lines to it. Flagged as growth only.
6. Design choice for the maintainer, not blocking: a drawn cone or arc is now shown as the stepped bands the laws judge, and an imported body shows its revolved envelope rather than its facets. The decision doc (`docs/decisions/743-sim-revolved-tool-body.md`) records this. The on-screen look was not hand-checked (the PR body says so).
7. Stacking: PR #843 is stacked on this branch. This review does not touch #843. Retarget it to `main` before this PR merges, per the stacked-PR rule.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
